name: TX-20
label: Safe D

key_factors: Castro's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge
Prediction markets price Castro near certain
No public polling and an underfunded, little-known challenger
model.rationale: Castro combines a strongly Democratic San Antonio-area seat with incumbency and a lopsided financial advantage, while prediction markets price his reelection at about 98 percent; nothing in the evidence points to a competitive race.
model.watch: Only an unexpected scandal or a surge of outside spending against Castro would move this forecast, since no polling exists to signal movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Joaquin Castro seeks another term in a San Antonio-area district that leans Democratic by about sixteen points. He enters the general election as the incumbent with a substantial financial edge, having raised more than ten times as much as Republican Edgardo Rafael Baez, whose campaign has modest cash on hand. Prediction markets put Castro's chances near certain, and no outside groups have invested in the race on either side.

No public general-election polling is available, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, incumbency, and money. Those factors all point the same way: a heavily Democratic seat, a well-known incumbent, and an underfunded challenger. The race is rated Safe Democratic, with Castro expected to win by a margin in the low twenties. The main uncertainty is the absence of polling rather than any sign of competition.
